subject: Vocabulary
topic: Antonyms — Advanced SSC-Level Vocabulary Pairs (W13 B1)

questions.stem: What is the antonym of LOQUACIOUS?
questions.explanation: C is correct. LOQUACIOUS = excessively talkative; using too many words. TACITURN = reserved; saying very little; temperamentally disinclined to talk. These are exact antonyms on the speech-quantity spectrum. Trap: verbose and garrulous = SYNONYMS of loquacious (both mean excessively wordy); talkative = also a synonym. Mnemonic: TACiturn = TACT of keeping quiet (silent).

questions.stem: What is the antonym of MENDACIOUS?
questions.explanation: B is correct. MENDACIOUS = not telling the truth; habitually dishonest; lying. TRUTHFUL = honest; telling the truth; veracious. Antonym pair: mendacious↔truthful. Root: Latin mendax = lying. Trap: deceptive, cunning, manipulative = all synonyms of mendacious (all involve dishonesty or trickery, not honesty).

questions.stem: What is the antonym of EBULLIENT?
questions.explanation: C is correct. EBULLIENT = cheerful and full of energy; overflowing with enthusiasm and excitement. DESPONDENT = in low spirits from loss of hope or courage; dejected. Direct antonyms on the energy/mood scale. Trap: enthusiastic, vivacious, exuberant = all synonyms of ebullient (high energy/positive mood). Mnemonic: EBULLIENT = bubbling over with joy (ebullition = boiling); DESPONDENT = deeply sinking in spirit.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of BENEVOLENT?
questions.explanation: B is correct. BENEVOLENT = well-meaning and kindly; wishing well to others (Latin bene = well + velle = to wish). MALEVOLENT = wishing evil to others; malicious (Latin male = badly + velle = to wish). These are exact Latin-rooted antonyms. Trap: charitable, munificent, philanthropic = synonyms of benevolent (all involve generosity or good will). The bene/male prefix pair is fundamental: benevolent↔malevolent, beneficial↔maleficent.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of PERSPICACIOUS?
questions.explanation: D is correct. PERSPICACIOUS = having a ready insight into things; shrewd; keenly perceptive. OBTUSE = annoyingly insensitive or slow to understand; lacking sharpness of mental acuity. Antonym pair: perceptive/sharp↔dull/slow-witted. Trap: shrewd, discerning, astute = all synonyms of perspicacious. Root of perspicacious: Latin perspicax = clear-sighted (per = through + specere = to look). Obtuse literally = blunt-angled (not sharp), applied to the mind = not sharp.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of TRUCULENT?
questions.explanation: C is correct. TRUCULENT = eager or quick to argue or fight; aggressively defiant. DOCILE = ready to accept control or instruction; submissive; easily managed. Antonym pair: aggressive/combative↔submissive/compliant. Trap: aggressive, belligerent, pugnacious = all synonyms of truculent (fighting-word cluster). Mnemonic: DOCILE = DOCks easily, follows instructions; TRUCULENT = like a truck barreling forward aggressively.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of TENACIOUS?
questions.explanation: C is correct. TENACIOUS = tending to keep a firm hold; not readily giving up; persistent. IRRESOLUTE = showing or feeling uncertainty about how to act; lacking resoluteness; wavering. Antonym pair: firm/persistent↔uncertain/wavering. Trap: persistent, resolute, determined = synonyms of tenacious. Root: TENACIOUS from Latin tenax = holding fast (tenere = to hold); IRRESOLUTE = not (ir-) resolved = unable to decide.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of MAGNANIMOUS?
questions.explanation: C is correct. MAGNANIMOUS = generous or forgiving, especially towards a rival or someone less powerful; noble in mind and spirit. PETTY = having or showing a small, mean, ungenerous spirit; trivially small-minded. Antonym pair: noble-spirited/generous↔small-minded/mean. Root: MAGNANIMOUS from Latin magnus (great) + animus (spirit). PETTY = Latin petitus (small). Trap: generous, noble, charitable = synonyms of magnanimous.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of PAROCHIAL?
questions.explanation: C is correct. PAROCHIAL = having a limited or narrow outlook confined to a local area; provincial (from 'parish' = local church district). COSMOPOLITAN = familiar with and at ease in many different countries and cultures; having a sophisticated, international outlook. Antonym pair: narrow local view↔broad global view. Trap: provincial, narrow-minded, insular = synonyms of parochial. Mnemonic: COSMOpolitan = COSMO (universe/world) + politan (citizen) = citizen of the world.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of PENURIOUS?
questions.explanation: C is correct. PENURIOUS = extremely poor; characterized by poverty. OPULENT = ostentatiously rich and luxurious; wealthy. Antonym pair: extremely poor↔extremely wealthy. Trap: miserly and parsimonious = about SPENDING little money (not necessarily about poverty — a miser can be rich but stingy); indigent = synonym of penurious (also extremely poor). SSC loves testing penurious because students confuse it with parsimonious (which is about spending, not wealth level).
